content: 1. Chapter and Microchapter Creation Guidelines Each microchapter should begin with the same base name as the main chapter. For instance, if the main chapter is about pericarditis, the microchapters should be titled Pericarditis overview, Pericarditis pathophysiology, Pericarditis treatment, and so on. Only the first word of each microchapter title should be capitalized. All microchapters listed in the template on the right-hand side of the main chapter should also appear on the home page of the main chapter. Each microchapter must include the template provided on the right-hand side of the page. It is not mandatory to create a microchapter for every title listed in the template. If certain titles are irrelevant to the condition being discussed, they should be removed from the microchapter template. For example, in the case of pericarditis, there may not be any primary or secondary prevention strategies, as primary prevention is not applicable to this condition. 2. The primary goal of this page is to provide a consumer-friendly overview of the condition, including its background, diagnosis, and treatment. The language should be simple enough for an 8th-grade reading level and should avoid overly technical terminology. The content should address the following key questions: What is the condition? What are the symptoms of the condition? What causes the condition? Who is at the highest risk of developing the condition? When should urgent medical care be sought? What are the available treatment options? Where can medical care for the condition be accessed? What is the expected prognosis or outlook for the condition? What are the possible complications associated with the condition? What are the sources of the information provided? Additionally, include a link to the corresponding WikiDoc page at the top of the patient information page. 3. Overview Section Guidelines The purpose of the overview section is to provide a concise summary of the condition, focusing on its background, diagnosis, and treatment. This section is particularly important as it will appear in Google search results, so it must be written with impeccable grammar and clarity. The content should include a general description of the condition's etiology, as well as a brief summary of its diagnostic and treatment approaches. Where applicable, links to more detailed microchapters should be included to guide readers to additional information. 4. Pathophysiology Section Guidelines The objective of the pathophysiology section is to explain the biological mechanisms underlying the disease. This section should include detailed descriptions of any embryological or developmental abnormalities, molecular or genetic abnormalities, and the pathogenesis of the condition. Pathology images should also be included where relevant. Efforts should be made to locate and include copyleft images of pathology specimens, as well as educational videos from platforms such as YouTube. Additional resources, such as the Pathology Wiki and Ask Dr. Wiki, should be consulted to find relevant images and materials to enhance the section.
